{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call-d5d361b1-e870-4d0c-9c26-2f923c48d65f-1","type":"tool_result","content":"1	# MonoCode Hub: how it works
2	
3	For the Monos and chats running inside the hub. Read the part you need; the tools' own descriptions have the details.
4	Asked how the hub works or what it shows, answer from this file and the hub's tools (`task_status`, `jobs.read`, `pages`). Don't read the app's source or tests to find out: it is slow and describes code, not what Ash sees. If this file doesn't say, say so in a line.
5	
6	## What Ash sees
7	- **Projects** are the unit of the hub; the strip on the left lists them. There is no area for all projects at once and no central board of every job.
8	- **A project's Today** is that project's home: the cards its template names (for example Since you were last here, Needs you), then **Being built**. Only a project has a Today; a Mono's chat, a room or a team has none, so never tell Ash something is "on Today" unless it is on that project's Today now.
9	- **Being built** lists that project's own live work only: its Lead's and coding team's open workers, grey while running, red only when Ash must act. It is not every job running anywhere.
10	- **Needs you** holds only what Ash himself must do (answer, allow, decide). Work a Lead recovered or retried by itself is not there.
11	- **Pages**: the pages kept in this install, each with Undo. Four ready-made pages that explain the basics come with every setup, once; one Ash removes is never put back. A page made with `page_build` shows him a preview first.
12	- **Teams** and **rooms**: each team has its own room; the Leadership room is the leadership Monos with Ash.
13	
14	## Who's who
15	- **Ash** talks to orchestrators only: a Mono's own chat, or a chat in a project's coding team. Workers never talk to him.
16	- **Monos** are long-lived agents with a soul (`SOUL.md`: who they are and what they own) and memory (`MEMORY.md` plus topic notes). The app keeps both; change them with the app CLI (`monocode app --help`: `soul.read`, `soul.update`, `memory.add`, `memory.replace`, `memory.search`). Never edit the Monos' home folder directly.
17	- **Project Leads** are Monos that own one project. Leadership Monos hand a project's work to its Lead (`delegate_task` with `lead`).
18	- **Workers** are chats you start with `delegate_task`. They see only your brief, so put the full job in it.
19	
20	## Handing work off
21	- `delegate_task` starts a worker; say in a line what you started and end your turn. Its report comes back to you as a `[MonoCode report]` turn, even after the app restarts. Its questions come as `[MonoCode question]`; answer with `task_answer`.
22	- A worker that is stuck or asks something only Ash can answer is yours to coordinate: ask Ash in your own chat, then pass his answer on with `task_answer`. Ash shouldn't have to open a worker's chat, and its questions never go to Chief of Staff.
23	- `task_status` reads progress and results, `task_wait` blocks on a short job, `task_cancel` stops a task and everything under it.
24	- About once an hour the app asks you to look at a worker that's been running an hour or more. Check it's really moving (commits, changed files, passing tests); if not, stop, split or retry it (`redoes`).
25	- `pr_watch` wakes you when a pull request you opened needs you.
26	
27	## Rooms (group chats)
28	- A room is a group chat with Ash and some Monos. Each message shows who wrote it. A Mono's words are never Ash's: don't save or quote them as his.
29	- When Ash writes, the host answers first. If he names nobody, every other seat then gets one turn to reply in its own voice. If he @names a seat (or opens with its name), only that seat answers.
30	- Reply `NO_REPLY` when you have nothing new; nothing is posted.
31	- Monos talk to each other only by naming a seat ("PM, ..."): that wakes it.
32	- One brake: after 20 Mono posts without Ash, the room pauses until he says keep going. The pause shows in a quiet strip above the composer, not as a message.
33	- Busy in your own chat when the room wakes you? Answer with `room_post`. Read with `room_read`. Private hand-offs go by `mono_message`.
34	
35	## The checker
36	After a chat answers one of Ash's long messages, the app takes one cheap look for anything that seems missed. If it finds something, the owning chat gets a private `[MonoCode check]` turn. Look, fix it if needed, and reply in one line starting `Right:` or `Fixed:`. The checker never starts work, and Ash doesn't see it.
37	
38	## Memory in Ash OS
39	Ash OS (`ash_recall` and friends) holds each project's decisions and Ash's global ones. Save to it (`ash_remember`) only when Ash says remember or lock.
40	
41	## What's shipped, what's stuck
42	Read it from the hub and the project's own checkout, never from GitHub: no `gh`, `git fetch` or anything else that goes online. Those wait on Ash's Allow card, and the hub already knows.
43	- Shipped: `git log --since="1 week ago"` in the project folder (local only).
44	- Stuck or still running: `task_status` (with no ids it also lists the team's other open jobs).
45	- On a page: the blocks filled from those, or a bespoke page that watches `jobs.read` (done jobs carry `finishedAt`) and `agents.read` (the stuck ones).
46	
47	## Habits
48	Things a Mono does on a schedule (hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly). Add one only once Ash agrees (`monocode app --help`, `habits`).
49	
50	## Making things with Ash: new Monos, teams, rooms, pages, hub changes
51	Ash can just ask any Mono for these in chat; nothing needs Settings.
52	- A new Mono: `mono_create`. Ask Ash at least one real question first, then draft it (name, role, who, what it watches for, skills). He sees a draft card; after his yes, call `mono_create` with only the `draftId` and it is made, shows in the sidebar, and gets a Bot changes row with Undo.
53	- A new team: `team_create`. Draft it with a name, a brief (what it is for), the projects it works on and the Monos that belong. He sees the team card in that chat; after his yes, call `team_create` with only the `draftId` and it is made, shows in Teams with its own room, and gets a Bot changes row with Undo (the team and its room go; its Monos stay). Never make or restructure staff any other way: a team goes in only on Ash's yes.
54	- A new room: `room_create`.
55	- Deleting a Mono: there is no tool for it, so no Mono deletes one. Ash does it himself: the Mono's ··· menu in the sidebar, Delete mono…, and the app asks him to confirm. A Mono made from chat can also be undone from its Bot changes row.
56	- A page: `page_build`. A change to the hub itself: `hub_change`.
57	Pages and hub changes show Ash a preview first; he clicks Apply or Discard, and anything applied can be undone in Bot changes.
58	
59	## Asking Ash
60	Decide what you can yourself. When you need him to choose, ask once, in your chat (AskUserQuestion), with your pick first. Deletes, money, anything sent as Ash, and anything irreversible need his yes.
